We are given σ = 40, n = 100, \overline{x}=780, and confidence level 1-\alpha=95\%=0.95 so \alpha=1-0.95=0.05, \frac{\alpha}{2}=\frac{0.05}{2}=0.025

Now make inverse use of area table of standard normal distribution and search 0.5 − 0.025 = 0.475 in the body of the table which correspond to Z_{\alpha/2}=Z_{0.025}=1.96.

Putting values in the above interval estimator, we get

780\pm 1.96\frac{40}{\sqrt{100}}

780\pm 1.96(4)

[772.16,\ 787.84]

Hence the 95% confidence interval for μ is from 772.16 to 787.84 hours.

Example 6.10

A random sample of size n = 400 selected without replacement from a population of size N = 2000 with σ = 4 gives \overline{x}=80. Use this sample information to construct a 90% confidence interval for the mean of the population.

Solution:

A 100 (1−α)% confidence interval for μ is \overline{X}\pm Z_{\alpha/2}\frac{\sigma}{\sqrt{n}}\sqrt{\frac{N-n}{N-1}}

Given that N = 2000, n = 400, σ = 4, \overline{x}=80,

$1-\alpha=0.90,\ \alpha=0.10,\ \frac{\alpha}{2}=0.05.$

From the area table we have Z_{\alpha/2}=Z_{0.05}=1.645 corresponding to the probability 0.50 − 0.05 = 0.45

Hence the 90% confidence interval for μ is

80\pm 1.645\frac{4}{\sqrt{400}}\sqrt{\frac{2000-400}{2000-1}}

\text{or } 80\pm 0.294

\text{or } 80-0.294,\ 80+0.294

\text{or } [79.706,\ 80.294]

Construct a 95% confidence interval for the mean daily intake of dairy products for males.

sections.theory:
6.3.3 Large sample confidence interval for population mean μ when σ is unknown

Practically, σ is usually not known but if n ≥ 30 then, central limit theorem allows us to consider the sampling distribution of \overline{X} as approximately normal with mean μ and S.E=\frac{s}{\sqrt{n}} that is, σ is replaced by sample standard deviation s. An approximate 100 (1−α)% confidence interval for μ in this case is given as;

$\overline{X}\pm Z_{\alpha/2}\frac{s}{\sqrt{n}}.$

Example 6.11

A scientist, interested in monitoring chemical contaminants in food, selected a random sample of n = 50 male adults. It was found that the average daily intake of dairy products was \overline{x}=756 grams per day with a standard deviation of s = 35 grams per day. Construct a 95% confidence interval for the mean daily intake of dairy products for males.

Solution:

Here σ is unknown but n = 50 is large, therefore, 100(1−α)% confidence interval for μ is:

$\overline{X}\pm Z_{\alpha/2}\frac{s}{\sqrt{n}}$

We have 1-\alpha=0.95, \alpha=0.05, Z_{\alpha/2}=Z_{0.025}=1.96

Hence the approximate 95% confidence interval for μ is

6.3.3 Large sample confidence interval for population mean μ when σ is unknown

Practically, σ is usually not known but if n ≥ 30 then, central limit theorem allows us to consider the sampling distribution of \overline{X} as approximately normal with mean μ and S.E=\frac{s}{\sqrt{n}} that is, σ is replaced by sample standard deviation s. An approximate 100 (1−α)% confidence interval for μ in this case is given as;

$\overline{X}\pm Z_{\alpha/2}\frac{s}{\sqrt{n}}.$
